name: Commission v France (C-636/18) (NO2)

jurisdiction.court: Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) – Seventh Chamber

description: Action brought by the Commission against France for the systematic and continuous exceedance of the annual (and in some cases hourly) limit value for NO2 in 12 agglomerations and zones (Paris, Marseille-Aix, Lyon, Grenoble, Strasbourg, Montpellier, Nice, Toulon, etc.) from 2010 to 2016 and for the failure to adopt plans under Article 23 of Directive 2008/50/EC that would reduce the period of exceedance “in the shortest possible time”.
outcome: Action upheld. The CJEU ruled against France. The judgment became one of the legal foundations of the French domestic litigation “Les Amis de la Terre”, which led to the multi-million astreintes (periodic penalty payments) imposed on the State by the Conseil d'État (French Council of State) between 2021 and 2023.
